sources.title: System Design Primer: Asynchronism, message queues, task queues and back pressure
sources.supportRationale: Required core conceptual/interview-study reference, inspected 2026-11-17; historical product comparisons are not adopted as current guarantees or evidence of question frequency.

sources.title: Apache Kafka 4.1: Design and delivery semantics
sources.supportRationale: Partitioned storage, publication/consumption semantics and scoped transaction boundaries; examples explicitly target the 4.1 series rather than a latest-version claim.

sources.title: Kafka Java client 4.1.2: KafkaConsumer
sources.supportRationale: Position versus committed position, manual progress handling, rebalances, thread-safety and asynchronous processing caveats.

sources.title: Apache Kafka 4.1: Consumer configuration
sources.supportRationale: Classic group, poll/progress, isolation and bounded-fetch controls; protocol and settings are named rather than inferred from generic consumer terminology.

sources.title: Apache Kafka 4.1: Producer configuration
sources.supportRationale: Acknowledgment, idempotence, retries, transaction identity and ordering constraints under explicit settings.

sources.title: RabbitMQ 4.1: Consumer acknowledgements and publisher confirms
sources.supportRationale: Independent publisher/consumer acknowledgment boundaries, manual versus automatic ack and requeue behavior in AMQP 0-9-1.

sources.title: RabbitMQ 4.1: Consumer prefetch
sources.supportRationale: Bounded unacknowledged deliveries and RabbitMQ-specific QoS scope; not a fleet-wide rate or business-transaction guarantee.

sources.title: AWS Prescriptive Guidance: Transactional outbox
sources.supportRationale: Atomic local state/publication intent and remaining duplicate/consumer effect boundaries.

scenarios.theme: A live presence hint is lost during a crash. Is retry required?
scenarios.assumptions: Another fresh hint arrives shortly and no consequential decision relies solely on the missing pulse. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A live presence hint is lost during a crash. Is retry required?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Accept the documented omission within its freshness budget, keep an authoritative refresh path and monitor loss/age

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: No retry lowers recovery overhead but loses intermediate observations

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: If each pulse becomes billing/audit input, change to recoverable delivery and safe processing.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to kdesign, kapi; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: A refund is missing after an offset commit. How do you redesign?
scenarios.assumptions: The consumer committed progress before calling the payment system and then crashed. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A refund is missing after an offset commit. How do you redesign?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Reconcile the missing refund and replace this loss-prone protocol with durable responsibility, stable provider operation identity and explicit uncertain-ou

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Retries can duplicate effects without provider support

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Faster processing narrows but never removes the crash gap; authoritative money movement cannot rely on that timing.

scenarios.theme: The progress commit times out. May the worker send the one-time effect?
scenarios.assumptions: The application cannot establish commit success or current ownership. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies At-Most-Once Delivery to commit unknown.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: The progress commit times out. May the worker send the one-time effect?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Stop that effect attempt and resolve progress/ownership using the supported consumer protocol, or use a stronger sink-side identity contract before proceed

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Stopping can omit work, which matches the chosen loss preference

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Proceeding blindly can allow both this worker and a replacement to act; a timeout is not proof of rejection.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to kapi, kconsumer; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: A single crash loses an entire batch. What do you change?
scenarios.assumptions: The measured omission burst exceeds the product’s disposable-sample loss budget. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies At-Most-Once Delivery to batch loss.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A single crash loses an entire batch. What do you change?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Reduce the precommitted unit and bound in-flight work, or adopt recoverable delivery if the required loss budget cannot be met by intentional omission.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Smaller commits reduce amortized throughput

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: No batch size makes the progress-before-effect crash window disappear.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to kapi; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: Two identical notifications arrive despite at-most-once consumption. Why?
scenarios.assumptions: A producer retried with a new record identity after an uncertain publish. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies At-Most-Once Delivery to producer repeat.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Two identical notifications arrive despite at-most-once consumption. Why?

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Trace both records and define stable business-intent identity at the producer/effect boundary when duplicate notification matters

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Deduplication needs retention and payload-conflict policy

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Two legitimate repeated notifications must not be collapsed just because their text matches.

scenarios.assumptions: The application acknowledged delivery automatically before completing durable work. What will you do and why?
